constraints.text: rowPresent => recState /= rsNone (unless forgot): no row outlives its record (no BadOrphan)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first two make delete_session / append_wtmp fail once and assert the record (status().sessions) stays while the row is still readable, then the next end removes row and record; the third asserts a second connection cannot recreate the row after the end

constraints.text: ttyOwner = tOld => recState /= rsNone (unless forgot): the name does not outlive the record
constraints.verifiedBy: both assert owner() is None after the end / the expiry

constraints.text: newLive => ttyOwner = tNew: an end never frees a name another session took (owner-checked release)
constraints.verifiedBy: the test releases the old session's reservation, reserves the name for kai:someone-else, ends the session, and asserts the owner is still kai:someone-else

constraints.text: outboxN + flightN + sessN + userN + shownN + lostN + strandedN = issuedN: an end files the held batch and drains the session inbox into the user's mailbox; a graceful stop files the outbox (and the mail of a read that settles) back to the relay; a stop whose bounded wait expires loses only the broadcast mail a late fetch takes; a process loss loses the outbox and the read in flight
constraints.verifiedBy: the first holds an unconfirmed batch (consuming relay) and asserts it is in the user mailbox after the end; the second asserts both inbox messages reach the user mailbox; the two tests of the graceful stop (test_shutdown_reads.py, test_claude_expiry.py) assert the stop side of the equation: the held batch and the settled read's mail are back in the relay. The loss side (a crash, a late broadcast fetch) has no test: see ProcessLoss and limitsWithoutTest. shownN is not asserted. flightN is asserted only through the first graceful-stop test (a read mid-fetch when the stop arrives)

constraints.text: recState = rsEnding => endRun = currentRun: a replaced run cannot end the session
constraints.verifiedBy: the end test: a connection of run a1 after a2 replaced it gets session_replaced (or is closed), row and owner are unchanged and one session remains; then the current run ends it. The ledger test shows the refusal is permanent

constraints.text: EndOwnSession: a connection of the current run begins the end
constraints.verifiedBy: end by the current-run connection removes row and name; a shell's session is refused invalid_params, which the model does not have (a stricter code)

constraints.text: EndRefused: a connection of a replaced run changes nothing
constraints.verifiedBy: after the refused end the test asserts row present, owner unchanged, one session in status

constraints.text: ExpireClaude: a dormant record with no connection, aged to retention, begins the end
constraints.verifiedBy: the first closes the client (no connection, dormant), a sweep at retention 3600 leaves it, a sweep at 0 removes row, name and record and appends one logout; the second shows a connected session is never expired; the third shows a reattached session is not expired (it shows the reattach wins, not that the age restarts from zero)

constraints.text: DeleteRow, ReleaseTty, AppendLogout, FileOutbox, FinishEnd: each effect of an end, and the record stays until all are done
constraints.verifiedBy: one test per effect; the failure tests make delete_session and append_wtmp fail once; the concurrency test parks the first end mid-effect and asserts one logout. A failure of the refile or the drain is not injected

constraints.text: NewHello: the new session of a clear takes the name only after the old end is complete (the goal needs an EndOwnSession step: ownEnded)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first test sends the old end, then the new hello, and asserts the name was free after the end and is then held by the new session; the second sends the new hello first and asserts its claim of the old name is refused while the old session holds it. The model's hello is the daemon-side name claim; the client's wait for the end's reply is not tested here

constraints.text: retention and end: enabled(ExpireClaude) at retention; every owed end step and the finish enabled; a failed end is finished by the next
constraints.verifiedBy: expiry at retention happens; a refused expiry leaves the record and the next sweep removes it; a failed end is finished by the next end

constraints.text: shownDormant = zfalse: held mail is not consumed when nobody is connected
constraints.verifiedBy: a reply is handed over (request_held), never confirmed, the client closes, a new connection reads and finds the message still unread. It shows no consumption without a confirming client, which is what the model's connected-client guard stands for

constraints.text: ProcessLoss (live or dormant): a crash loses the daemon's outbox and any read in flight; the relay's mail is not lost (PL-1753)
constraints.verifiedBy: no test. A crash cannot be tested in-process: the daemon test harness stops a daemon gracefully, and a graceful stop now files the outbox back. The only test that asserted an outbox loss (test_a_daemon_restart_loses_the_outbox_but_not_the_relays_mail) was removed with the hand-back, because what it stopped was a graceful stop. Counted as uncovered

constraints.text: GracefulStop / GracefulStopForget (settled? = ztrue): the held outbox of every session, and mail of a read that settled, is filed back to the relay before the daemon closes; the relay's mail is untouched
constraints.verifiedBy: read on main 5684388. The first: a consuming relay whose fetch_user_inbox consumes the mail and stalls 0.3 s; harness.daemon.stop() is called while a read is mid-fetch (consumed set); a new BiffDaemon queried by a cli client returns the mail: the settle step waits for the read and the hand-over files it. The second is parametrised over consuming and non-consuming relays: a seat holds an unconfirmed batch (request_held 'read'), the daemon is stopped and revived, and a reattached read returns it. The third holds three unconfirmed messages, makes the first publish at stop fail, and asserts m2 and m3 are given back (one refused message does not drop the rest; the refused one stays held and is logged). All restart a daemon that has forgotten its harness records, so they exercise GracefulStopForget, not the durable GracefulStop; the filing is the same step

constraints.text: GracefulStop / GracefulStopForget (settled? = zfalse, lastStop = sTimedOut): the settle wait is bounded and the stop returns; held mail is filed back; mail the read had not yet taken stays in the relay; session mail already in the outbox survives
constraints.verifiedBy: the first sets SETTLE_SECONDS to 0.1, holds m1 (request_held), writes m2, and starts a read that hangs before taking m2; stop() completes inside 0.4 s and a restarted daemon reads m1 and m2 (m1 filed back, m2 never taken). The second makes the broadcast fetch stick after the session fetch took the session mail; stop() runs out the wait and a restarted daemon reads the session mail (SessionFetch put it into the outbox before the broadcast fetch). Neither test makes a fetch consume mail and then outlive the wait: that loss (lostN with sTimedOut) is the window PL-1777 tracks, see limitsWithoutTest

limitsWithoutTest.text: GracefulStop with settled? = zfalse and mail in flight (lostN > 0, lastStop = sTimedOut): a read whose broadcast fetch consumed the user's mail and outlives the settle wait loses it
limitsWithoutTest.reason: the window the code cannot close without a further change (PL-1777: the late broadcast fetch). The session mail is not in it: SessionFetch holds it in the outbox first, which test_session_mail_a_read_took_before_a_stuck_broadcast_fetch_survives_a_stop asserts. No test asserts the loss itself, because it would pin a defect. The model's loss is of the broadcast fetch only (BroadcastFetch, flightN); the session fetch (MailFetch) enters the outbox atomically

limitsWithoutTest.text: Handback refile budget (REFILE_SECONDS, 15 s) spent: the held messages not yet filed are dropped and logged
limitsWithoutTest.reason: the deadline remainder is lost with the process (PL-1777). test_slow_publishes_at_stop_end_at_a_total_budget_and_are_logged asserts the stop ends at the budget and logs the count, not that the remainder survives. The model has no transition for it yet: a spill transition (the remainder written to local storage) will be modelled with the fix

limitsWithoutTest.text: ProcessLoss: the crash loses the outbox and any read in flight (PL-1753), and the forgotten harness records (PL-1771)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: counted as a GAP in the summary, not as covered: a crash cannot be tested in-process, and the only test that asserted an outbox loss was removed with the hand-back. The loss is kept in the model as ProcessLoss and ProcessLossForget

limitsWithoutTest.text: GracefulStopForget, ProcessLossForget, RowAgesOut, TtyAgesOut: the code keeps harness records in memory, so a restart forgets them; the row and (on NATS) the name age out by the relay's lifetime, the local relay's name reservation has no lifetime, and the restarted session's own relay inbox is stranded (strandedN; the user's mailbox is untouched)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: a divergence from the durable-record model, reported as a finding (PL-1771 tracks the code fix): a name held up to the row lifetime, or for good on the local relay, and unread session-inbox mail never drained to the user mailbox. No test asserts the forgotten record or the stranding

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-unordered-owned.tex: the owner check alone keeps the new session's name
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (2,351 states, invariant holds); the code's check is covered by test_a_name_another_session_took_is_not_freed_by_the_end

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-nograceful.tex: a graceful stop that skips the hand-back violates conservation
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (50 states to the violation; counterexample MailArrive, MailFetch, GracefulStopForget); the code's hand-back is covered by the graceful-stop tests above

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-noflight.tex and -noflight-counted.tex: a settled stop that drops the read's mail (uncounted: conservation is violated; counted: lastStop = sGraceful => stopLost = 0 is violated)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model results (the first violates invariant 8, the second invariant 13); the code files the settled read's mail, covered by the first test of the graceful-stop row
